sentence: This project uses stem cell-based models of human central nervous system development to study key molecular and cellular events early in that development.
This project builds an imaging system that uses deep learning to detect cancerous tissue and map physiological parameters during robot-assisted prostate surgery.
This project studies how one factor limits chronic pancreatitis by suppressing fibro-inflammatory responses, using human samples and transgenic mouse models.
This project uses interactions between proteins and nanoparticles to study how different cells in the ovarian tumor microenvironment communicate.
This project develops ways to use whole-genome sequencing and RNA sequencing of blood cell types to find genetic causes of rare diseases.
This project studies the molecular and cellular steps that start tooth development, especially the regulatory networks that drive dental lamina fate.
This project studies how regulatory DNA sequences tune gene expression and how to engineer them to restore function in Alagille Syndrome.
This project builds a compact intraoral camera with four imaging modalities to detect and diagnose caries and crack.
This project builds a robotic system with artificial intelligence that positions a magnetic brain stimulation device with millimeter precision and learns in real-time.
This project supplies mutant mouse strains and generates new mutant mouse strains for immunological research.
This project looks for biomarkers of limbal stem cell deficiency in cultivated limbal stem cells, tears, and images analyzed with deep learning.
This project gives cancer researchers help with biostatistics, bioinformatics and clinical trial support, and develops methods for microbiome data analysis.
This project studies a group of highly functional regulatory T cells to find how they suppress the immune response in pancreatic cancer.
This project studies how adult stem cells in the Drosophila ovary are maintained and how signaling pathways control their proliferation and competition.
This project practices responding to foodborne illness outbreaks through tabletop exercises and a centralized system for collecting complaints.
This project studies the genetic basis of pediatric gastrointestinal, liver, and nutritional disease.
This project combines multiplexed tissue imaging, spatial transcriptomics and artificial intelligence to build a tool that predicts melanoma recurrence.
This project studies how acute myeloid leukemia cells interact with their niche to promote disease progression.
This project studies how a transcription factor guides development of chemosensory neurons in the hindbrain that control breathing.
